memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "Then Moses left Pharaoh and prayed to the Lord, and the Lord did what Moses asked. The flies left Pharaoh and his officials and his people; not a fly remained. But this time also Pharaoh hardened his heart and would not let the people go." - Exodus 8:30-32 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
God answers thoroughly — not a fly remained. And Pharaoh hardens his heart again.

We have now seen this cycle three times in one chapter: crisis, plea, relief, refusal. The phrase this time also tells us the pattern is established. What was once a decision has become a habit.

That is how hearts harden. Not usually in one dramatic act of rebellion, but through repetition. Each refusal makes the next one easier and more automatic.

The warning for us is real. If we repeatedly feel conviction and repeatedly ignore it, the conviction eventually stops coming. Paul speaks of a conscience that can become seared (1 Tim 4:2).

But notice the other half of this verse: not a fly remained. God's faithfulness did not depend on Pharaoh's integrity. God did exactly what He said, even for a man who would break his word again within the hour.

Our God keeps His word to people who do not keep theirs. That is grace, and it is our only hope.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. What cycle in my life keeps repeating, and what would break it?
2. Have I thanked God for keeping His word to me when I have not kept mine?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Faithful Lord, thank You for keeping Your word even when I break mine. Break the cycles in me that I cannot break myself. Amen.
